spf_fail.name: SPF Authentication Failure
spf_fail.description: Originating sending IP is not authorized in sender domain's SPF DNS record.
spf_fail.why_it_matters: Enables malicious actors to forge sender envelope domains and bypass standard server identity checks.

spf_softfail.name: SPF Policy Softfail
spf_softfail.description: Originating sending IP is discouraged by sender domain's SPF policy.
spf_softfail.why_it_matters: Indicates questionable relay path or misconfigured forwarding; frequently weaponized for spoofing.

dkim_fail.name: DKIM Signature Verification Failed
dkim_fail.description: Cryptographic signature failed mathematical verification or email body was modified in transit.
dkim_fail.why_it_matters: Email contents may have been tampered with by an intermediate relay or sent from unauthorized systems.

dmarc_fail.name: DMARC Policy Alignment Failed
dmarc_fail.description: Sender header domain is unaligned with both verified SPF and DKIM identifiers.
dmarc_fail.why_it_matters: Primary mechanism for executive display and organization domain impersonation.

display_name_spoof.name: Display Name Spoofing Detected
display_name_spoof.description: Human-facing display name claims identity of a known brand or VIP, but sending domain is unrelated.
display_name_spoof.why_it_matters: Deceives human recipients into trusting malicious instructions by mimicking legitimate contacts.

reply_to_mismatch.name: Reply-To Destination Mismatch
reply_to_mismatch.description: Reply-To header routes responses to an entirely distinct domain from the apparent From sender.
reply_to_mismatch.why_it_matters: Redirects victim replies to adversary-controlled inboxes during BEC and credential collection attacks.

return_path_mismatch.name: Return-Path Envelope Mismatch
return_path_mismatch.description: SMTP envelope bounce return path does not match From header domain.
return_path_mismatch.why_it_matters: Frequently indicates spam relaying, hijacked accounts, or unaligned bulk mail infrastructure.

brand_impersonation.name: Brand Lookalike Domain Impersonation
brand_impersonation.description: Domain mimics a protected brand using homoglyphs, typosquatting, or character substitution.
brand_impersonation.why_it_matters: Designed to establish visual deception so users fail to notice subtle spelling differences.

url_high_risk.name: High-Risk Malicious URL Structure
url_high_risk.description: URL exhibits multiple suspicious static signals (IP host, punycode, deep subdomains, credential targets).
url_high_risk.why_it_matters: Directs victims to credential harvesting landing pages or malware drops.

url_suspicious.name: Suspicious URL Observed
url_suspicious.description: Extracted hyperlink exhibits abnormal length, token obfuscation, or unusual character density.
url_suspicious.why_it_matters: Commonly used in phased redirect chains to evade signature-based URL scanners.

html_link_mismatch.name: HTML Display Link Mismatch
html_link_mismatch.description: Visible text inside anchor tag displays one domain while href directs user to a different destination.
html_link_mismatch.why_it_matters: Classical phishing tactic to visually reassure victim while surreptitiously redirecting them.

domain_age_under_7d.name: Domain Registered Under 7 Days Ago
domain_age_under_7d.description: Domain was newly registered within the past week.
domain_age_under_7d.why_it_matters: Adversaries regularly register throwaway domains immediately before executing phishing campaigns.

newly_registered_domain.name: Newly Registered Domain (<30 Days)
newly_registered_domain.description: Domain was registered within the past 30 days.
newly_registered_domain.why_it_matters: New domains lack historical reputation and are statistical outliers for legitimate corporate correspondence.

suspicious_tld.name: High-Risk / Low-Cost TLD
suspicious_tld.description: Domain utilizes top-level domain frequently associated with automated abuse and disposable spam.
suspicious_tld.why_it_matters: Low registration cost and weak registrar verification make these TLDs attractive for mass phishing.

dns_anomaly.name: DNS Architecture Anomaly
dns_anomaly.description: Domain lacks standard MX records, proper nameservers, or exhibits unresolvable DNS configuration.
dns_anomaly.why_it_matters: Indicates ephemeral infrastructure or non-standard routing setup common in disposable attack campaigns.

credential_request.name: Credential Harvesting Language
credential_request.description: Email body contains urgent phrases instructing recipient to verify, reset, or submit login credentials.
credential_request.why_it_matters: Primary behavioral indicator of account takeover and credential theft campaigns.

financial_language.name: Urgent Financial / Wire Request
financial_language.description: Email body solicits wire transfers, invoice adjustments, gift cards, or cryptocurrency payments.
financial_language.why_it_matters: Primary behavioral vector for Business Email Compromise (BEC) and payroll diversion fraud.

urgency_language.name: Artificial Urgency & Coercion Phrasing
urgency_language.description: Email creates psychological pressure with immediate deadlines (e.g. 'account closed in 24 hours').
urgency_language.why_it_matters: Short-circuits victim skepticism and prevents recipient from seeking out-of-band verification.

suspicious_attachment_extension.name: Dangerous Executable or Script Attachment
suspicious_attachment_extension.description: Email carries attachment with dangerous extension (.exe, .iso, .vbs, .bat, .hta, etc.).
suspicious_attachment_extension.why_it_matters: Direct vehicle for initial access, loader execution, and ransomware payload staging.

attachment_macro_payload.name: Macro-Enabled Office Document
attachment_macro_payload.description: Attachment contains VBA macros (.docm, .xlsm) capable of remote process execution.
attachment_macro_payload.why_it_matters: Used to drop remote access trojans (RATs) and stage living-off-the-land attacks.

executable_disguised_as_document.name: Executable Disguised as Document
executable_disguised_as_document.description: Attachment filename claims document format but magic bytes reveal a Windows PE executable or script.
executable_disguised_as_document.why_it_matters: Classic adversary defense evasion and social engineering technique to trick users into running binaries.

pdf_suspicious_actions.name: PDF Suspicious Execution Elements
pdf_suspicious_actions.description: PDF contains active elements such as /JavaScript, /OpenAction, /Launch, or embedded payload files.
pdf_suspicious_actions.why_it_matters: Frequently utilized in drive-by downloads and reader exploitation to execute payloads without user interaction.

double_extension_detected.name: Double Extension Evasion
double_extension_detected.description: Attachment uses dual extensions (e.g. .pdf.exe or .docx.vbs) to camouflage dangerous payloads.
double_extension_detected.why_it_matters: Exploits standard operating system hidden extension defaults to trick victims.

archive_with_hidden_executable.name: Archive Packaging Hidden Executables
archive_with_hidden_executable.description: Archive safely inspected and discovered containing executable or script payloads (.exe, .scr, .bat).
archive_with_hidden_executable.why_it_matters: Bypasses perimeter mail gateway filters that permit zip archives while blocking raw binaries.

path_traversal_archive_exploit.name: Archive Path Traversal (Zip Slip)
path_traversal_archive_exploit.description: Archive entry contains path traversal characters (../) targeting arbitrary file overwrite.
path_traversal_archive_exploit.why_it_matters: High-impact exploit attempting to drop files outside the extraction directory into system startup paths.

password_protected_suspicious_archive.name: Password-Protected Archive Evasion
password_protected_suspicious_archive.description: Attachment archive is encrypted with password protection, preventing automated perimeter inspection.
password_protected_suspicious_archive.why_it_matters: Commonly paired with phishing text providing the password to bypass corporate email gateways.

unsigned_executable.name: Unsigned Windows Executable
unsigned_executable.description: Binary lacks valid Authenticode cryptographic code-signing certificate.
unsigned_executable.why_it_matters: Legitimate enterprise software is typically signed; untrusted binaries pose substantial threat risk.

embedded_phishing_url_in_attachment.name: Embedded Phishing Links in Attachment
embedded_phishing_url_in_attachment.description: Static analysis detected external phishing URLs or credential harvester links inside attachment streams.
embedded_phishing_url_in_attachment.why_it_matters: Shifts malicious link hosting into documents to evade inline email body URL scanners.

high_entropy_packed_binary.name: High-Entropy Packed Binary
high_entropy_packed_binary.description: Executable exhibits Shannon entropy exceeding 7.5, indicating software packing, cryptors, or obfuscation.
high_entropy_packed_binary.why_it_matters: Indicates active evasion against signature-based antivirus solutions.

suspicious_ip_hosting_or_proxy.name: Anonymization Relay (Proxy/VPN/Tor/Datacenter)
suspicious_ip_hosting_or_proxy.description: Sending relay IP is a classified commercial proxy, Tor exit node, or unassigned hosting space.
suspicious_ip_hosting_or_proxy.why_it_matters: Obfuscates true adversary origin and evades geographic blocking policies.

known_campaign_match.name: Correlated Campaign Infrastructure
known_campaign_match.description: Email shares IOCs, sending IP subnets, or brand targeting with cataloged attack campaigns.
known_campaign_match.why_it_matters: Links isolated email events to coordinated multi-target adversary campaigns.

shared_malicious_infrastructure.name: Shared Malicious ASN / Hosting Provider
shared_malicious_infrastructure.description: Hosting ASN matches known bulletproof hosting providers repeatedly observed in malicious campaigns.
shared_malicious_infrastructure.why_it_matters: Indicates deliberate selection of hosting providers that ignore abuse complaints.

ml_phishing_signal.name: NLP Model Phishing Risk Assessment
ml_phishing_signal.description: Machine learning text model classified body semantics as high phishing probability (>=75%).
ml_phishing_signal.why_it_matters: Provides statistical corroboration of social engineering rhetoric.

spf_pass.name: Verified SPF Authorization
spf_pass.description: Originating sending IP is explicitly authorized in domain's published SPF policy.

dkim_pass.name: Valid Cryptographic DKIM Signature
dkim_pass.description: Email contains valid cryptographic signature proving sender authenticity and body integrity.
dkim_pass.why_it_matters: Proves message was not altered in transit and originated from signing domain.

dmarc_pass.name: DMARC Policy Alignment Verified
dmarc_pass.description: From header domain aligns with verified SPF and/or DKIM authentication results.
dmarc_pass.why_it_matters: Provides highest degree of domain ownership confidence against spoofing.

established_domain.name: Well-Established Domain History
established_domain.description: Sender domain has been registered for over 1 year with continuous operational reputation.
established_domain.why_it_matters: Significantly decreases probability of disposable phishing infrastructure.

clean_urls.name: Extracted URLs Exhibit Normal Baseline
clean_urls.description: All inspected hyperlinks conform to legitimate structure without obfuscation or redirection.
clean_urls.why_it_matters: Absence of suspicious link structures reduces likelihood of credential harvesting destination.

safe_attachments.name: Attachments Free of Executables/Macros
safe_attachments.description: Inspected attachments are standard non-executable document types without embedded macros.
safe_attachments.why_it_matters: Reduces immediate malicious payload execution risk.

trusted_sender_history.name: Consistent Sender Identity
trusted_sender_history.description: Sender headers (From, Reply-To, Return-Path) are perfectly aligned without spoofing markers.
trusted_sender_history.why_it_matters: Absence of identity mismatch indicators supports legitimate communication.

ml_low_risk_content.name: NLP Content Assessment Indicates Benign Text
ml_low_risk_content.description: Machine learning model evaluated textual phrasing as low phishing risk (<=15%).
ml_low_risk_content.why_it_matters: Supports benign intent of written communication.
